sourceEvidence.label: nexID base revision, active sprint source, migrations, and focused security regressions

assessment.summary: The evidence supports an owned tenant-authority boundary and a reusable durable external-effect lifecycle; tactical IAM, dashboard, IOTA, and webhook fixes remain necessary during migration.

nonNegotiables: Non-super administrative principals never receive global tenant scope.
A durable intent exists before a privileged external effect.
No production web workload holds an exportable blockchain signer key.
Existing tactical isolation and verification guards remain during migration.
assumptions: The Next.js and PostgreSQL monorepo remains the near-term control plane.
No measured authorization, queue throughput, latency, memory, RPO, or RTO budget was supplied.
The active sprint diff is not deployed and its database migrations have not been applied.

opportunities.title: Centralize tenant authority
opportunities.summary: Make global versus tenant authority a typed, current, and repository-owned decision instead of a page and route convention.
opportunities.diagnosis: Root credentials, session snapshots, tenant headers, role branches, and route-local SQL historically interpreted authority independently, allowing successful authentication to outlive or widen the intended tenant decision.

evidence.claim: IAM mutations require create-only identity handling and atomic tenant ownership checks to prevent cross-tenant account takeover.
Privileged session use must revalidate current user, membership, and permission state rather than trust stale snapshots.
Dashboard feature pages needed one policy that reserves global scope for super-admin and binds every other role to the session tenant.
The repeated forced-scope regression matrix indicates a structural control-ownership problem, not one isolated missing predicate.

desiredInvariants: Only a current super-admin principal can obtain global administrative scope.
Every other administrative principal has one current, non-empty tenant before upstream access.
Status, membership, role, and permissions are current at privileged use time.
Resource ownership and mutation remain atomic inside the database boundary.
Tenant repositories cannot be called without an explicit tenant principal.

options.title: Strengthened local guards
options.summary: Keep the current architecture and close each demonstrated page, route, session, and mutation path locally.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Create-only and row-locked ownership CTEs are the direct fix.
Current entitlement checks close the demonstrated stale-session path.
BFF-only pages and a central dashboard scope helper remove the ambient root path.
Focused guards close known routes but future callers can repeat the class.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known IAM and tenant-scope paths fail closed, although the invariant can drift at new call sites.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the full role-by-resource override matrix and static page credential gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: No network hop is added; current-IAM checks add bounded database work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure authorization p50, p95, p99 and connection use at realistic concurrency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Guards retain only bounded principal and query values.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare process RSS under the authorization load test.

tradeoffs.assessment: Revoked access stops promptly, but route-local failure behavior remains heterogeneous.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fail the IAM dependency and verify consistent fail-closed behavior and timeouts.

tradeoffs.assessment: No service is added, but many regression gates remain necessary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Track guard ownership, denial reasons, and route coverage in CI.

tradeoffs.assessment: The fixes preserve existing APIs and can ship incrementally.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run compatibility suites for legitimate tenant and super-admin workflows.

residualRisks: A new page or SQL caller can omit the local guard.
Background jobs and super-admin service principals remain separately governed.

workPackages: Preserve the tactical IAM and dashboard patches.
Keep static and role-matrix regression gates mandatory.
acceptanceCriteria: No non-super role can force or receive another tenant or global scope.
IAM ownership races cannot mutate a foreign identity.
migrationNotes: Ship before structural migration because it is direct containment.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert only an individual compatibility regression; do not restore ambient root credentials or permissive ownership behavior.

options.title: One owned tenant-authority boundary
options.summary: Resolve one typed current principal and require it at BFF, application-service, and tenant-repository boundaries.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Owned resource resolution reduces recurrence; atomic mutations remain required.
The final principal is constructed from current entitlements.
The BFF becomes the only feature-page transport for privileged data.
Repository signatures make missing tenant scope explicit and exceptional.

tradeoffs.assessment: The authority decision stays explicit across layers and unscoped tenant access becomes difficult to express.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add contract tests for typed principals and reject unscoped repository calls statically.

tradeoffs.assessment: In-process policy avoids a network hop, while current entitlement resolution still costs database work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark against the local-guard baseline before setting release thresholds.

tradeoffs.assessment: Typed principals are small; any entitlement cache must be bounded and versioned.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cache cardinality and RSS, including tenant churn.

tradeoffs.assessment: One owned failure policy replaces route-specific widening, but the BFF and resolver become critical paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise database/cache outage, timeout, and break-glass scenarios.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central decisions support consistent denial telemetry and fewer enforcement owners.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify actor, tenant, action, resource, policy version, and outcome metrics.

tradeoffs.assessment: Direct SQL and direct API callers must move behind typed services or repositories.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory callers and migrate highest-risk domains with dual-decision logging.

residualRisks: Raw SQL outside the repository boundary can bypass the type system.
Super-admin abuse, database operators, and background service principals remain privileged.

workPackages: Build scoped repositories and explicit global interfaces.
Migrate high-risk domains and add policy telemetry.
acceptanceCriteria: Only a current super-admin can construct GlobalPrincipal.
Legacy and central policy never grant on disagreement.
migrationNotes: Preserve local guards until every caller is migrated.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Roll back one repository adapter while retaining BFF-only transport and tactical guards.

options.title: External policy decision service
options.summary: Move versioned authorization decisions to a dedicated policy service while keeping local enforcement and tenant predicates.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Central policy helps ownership decisions; database atomicity remains local.
Current identity inputs and invalidation remain prerequisites.
The transport must still remove ambient root credentials.
Local enforcement points must still bind the decision to final resources.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cross-service policy can converge, but decision centralization does not enforce database predicates by itself.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run policy/resource drift and obligation-enforcement tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: A network decision or cache enters each privileged request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure uncached and cached p50, p95, p99 under outage and load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Policy bundles, decision caches, and a service process consume additional bounded resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure service and enforcement-point RSS across policy versions.

tradeoffs.assessment: PDP outage, cache staleness, and policy/application drift create new failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Chaos-test fail-closed behavior, emergency policy, and version skew.

tradeoffs.assessment: Independent policy deployment, SLOs, promotion, and incident response become mandatory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse policy rollback, break-glass, and decision-log investigation.

tradeoffs.assessment: The application still needs the owned enforcement boundary plus dual-run policy migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Shadow decisions and require zero grant mismatches before cutover.

residualRisks: A correct policy decision can still be applied to the wrong resource.
Availability and policy-version drift become security dependencies.

acceptanceCriteria: Policy outage fails closed within a bounded timeout.
Decision and enforcement resource identities match.
Rollback restores the last verified policy without widening access.
migrationNotes: Prefer only after multiple independently deployed control planes need the same policy.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Pin the last verified bundle or fall back to the owned in-process policy without removing local enforcement.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the owned boundary under the current monorepo constraints, while preserving the completed local guards throughout migration.

opportunities.title: Make privileged external effects durable and capability-scoped
opportunities.summary: Give blockchain publication, tenant webhook egress, and critical audit a common durable-intent, leased-attempt, and independently verified lifecycle.
opportunities.diagnosis: Inline chain, network, and audit effects historically had different crash windows and ambient capabilities even though all require precommitted identity, bounded retries, reconciliation, and explicit confirmation semantics.

evidence.claim: IOTA V2 now demonstrates deterministic proof identity, durable attempts, broadcast identity persistence, and independent chain reconciliation.
Tenant-controlled webhook destinations require DNS-complete address policy, pinned TLS egress, response bounds, leases, retries, and dead letters.
The current audit helper catches database failure, so privileged business success can exist without durable audit evidence.
Domain-specific attempt, delivery, and audit tables make staged convergence possible without a platform rewrite.

desiredInvariants: A deterministic identity or idempotency key exists before every privileged external effect.
Durable intent commits before broadcast, egress, or irreversible mutation.
A crash after remote acceptance can reconcile without blind duplication.
Workers use atomic leases, bounded backoff, terminal states, and tenant/provider limits.
Signer, unrestricted egress, and immutable audit are separate capabilities.
Confirmation is independently verified and never inferred from mutable local status alone.

options.title: Hardened feature-local state machines
options.summary: Keep domain tables and workers while enforcing the same idempotency, lease, retry, verification, and capability rules in each domain.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The V2 writer and reconciler are the direct chain fix.
The outbox worker and DNS-pinned egress close the demonstrated SSRF and inline-delivery path.
Critical action policy still needs transactional or outbox-backed audit.
Existing domain persistence is reused rather than replaced.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known chain and webhook boundaries gain durable identity and scoped capabilities, while audit remains a declared follow-up.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Repeat crash-window, SSRF, receipt, calldata, event, storage, and confirmation tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: SDK and admin requests stop waiting on tenant egress or chain finality; workers add database work off-path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure request latency, queue age, DB connections, and worker throughput.

tradeoffs.assessment: Leased batches and bounded responses cap per-worker memory, while queued rows consume durable storage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure worker RSS and table growth at 1x and 10x pilot volume.

tradeoffs.assessment: Effects recover after process failure and preserve terminal evidence instead of disappearing with a request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures before and after broadcast, remote response, and local acknowledgement.

tradeoffs.assessment: Schedulers, secrets, queue-age alerts, DLQ review, and reconciliation runbooks become mandatory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse worker outage, stale-lease recovery, and DLQ triage.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each domain can canary independently using its existing schema and kill switch.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deploy disabled workers, reconcile pending rows, and canary one tenant/provider.

residualRisks: Retry and lease primitives can drift between domains.
The private-key executor is not enterprise key custody.
Critical audit is still best-effort until explicitly migrated.

workPackages: Deploy webhook worker and egress policy.
Classify and migrate critical audit actions.
acceptanceCriteria: One logical effect survives every tested crash window.
No prohibited webhook destination opens a socket.
Database status alone never claims external confirmation.
migrationNotes: Historical IOTA V1 remains read-only; old failed webhooks enter dead-letter rather than surprise replay.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable workers while retaining queued intent and evidence; never delete or mark pending effects successful.

options.title: Shared transactional outbox and capability adapters
options.summary: Standardize intent, lease, retry, terminal evidence, and metrics while leaving domain adapters responsible for confirmation semantics.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: IOTA exact verification remains domain-specific while intent lifecycle is standardized.
Egress validation stays mandatory inside the webhook adapter.
Critical audit intent can commit transactionally with the business mutation.
Domain tables can dual-write digests during staged migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: One lifecycle reduces recurrence, but adapters must keep strict domain validation and least-privilege capabilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use conformance tests plus domain-specific SSRF and chain verification suites.

tradeoffs.assessment: Shared polling can batch efficiently or create one hot queue depending on indexes and fairness.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Load-test queue scans, locks, tenant fairness, and adapter saturation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bounded leases keep worker memory stable; generic payloads can increase durable storage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure payload size, retention, partition growth, and worker RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unified leases and telemetry simplify recovery, but a shared queue can couple noisy tenants or adapters.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test per-tenant/provider quotas, poison messages, and adapter isolation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Queue age, attempts, DLQ, and reconciliation metrics become consistent across integrations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run incident drills using the shared dashboard and runbook.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each domain needs shadow dual-write and terminal-state comparison before cutover.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require digest and terminal-state parity without double-sending.

residualRisks: A shared queue can become a cross-domain availability dependency.
Sensitive payload retention and tenant fairness require explicit policy.

workPackages: Define generic intent and adapter contract.
Add quotas, retention, and adapter kill switches.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain and shared terminal states remain equivalent in shadow mode.
No adapter can use another adapter's capability.
migrationNotes: Cut one adapter at a time and preserve domain evidence tables during validation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop shared consumption and resume the domain worker from preserved intent without replaying confirmed effects.

options.title: Isolated publication, egress, and audit services
options.summary: Run signer, network egress, and immutable audit capabilities under separate service identities and infrastructure controls.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Non-exportable signer custody narrows chain-key authority; exact V2 verification remains required.
A network-restricted egress service contains SSRF impact; destination validation remains required.
An append-only external sink survives application database compromise.
Existing persistence feeds queues and services during migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service identities, KMS, network policy, and WORM storage sharply reduce ambient capability in feature code.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test identity policy, denied cross-capability calls, key extraction resistance, and immutable retention.

tradeoffs.assessment: Queue and service hops add latency and throughput limits to effect processing.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end queue-to-confirmation latency under peak fanout.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separate runtimes and queues add baseline process and buffering overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-service RSS, autoscaling floor, and queue buffer growth.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, while more services, identities, and queues expand the outage surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run regional, queue, KMS, DNS, and sink outage drills with recovery objectives.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each capability needs deployment, on-call, SLO, rotation, replay, and disaster-recovery ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require owner, runbook, alerts, restore drill, and access review before production.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service contracts, identities, network policy, KMS integration, and queue replay require staged cutover.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Canary one capability and region, rehearse rollback, then expand.

residualRisks: KMS policy abuse and queue operator access can still authorize harmful effects.
More infrastructure can reduce availability without disciplined ownership and drills.

workPackages: Select custody and regional operating model.
Build replay, rotation, and disaster-recovery controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Web workloads cannot export or invoke raw signer keys.
Egress can reach only approved public destinations.
Critical audit evidence survives application database compromise.
migrationNotes: Adopt first for mainnet key custody, restricted egress, and regulated audit rather than extracting every adapter.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Pause queue consumption and restore the last verified local adapter only if its capability boundary remains acceptable for the environment.

opportunities.recommendation: Complete the feature-local containment already in the sprint, then converge on a shared outbox; isolate signer, egress, and audit capabilities when mainnet, regulated data, or measured scale justifies the operational cost.

openQuestions: Are reseller principals single-tenant or organization-scoped with an explicit tenant allowlist?
Which privileged actions must fail closed when durable audit evidence is unavailable?
What throughput, latency, queue-age, RPO, and RTO objectives apply to the first enterprise pilot?
Which KMS/HSM, egress, and immutable-audit operating model is approved for mainnet and regulated workloads?
